cards.text: Jesus is speaking to the people again, and He opens with this: "I am the light of the world." Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer. When somebody says light, I'm LISTENING.

cards.question: Jesus says He is the light of the world. What does He promise whoever follows Him?

answers.text: They will never walk in the darkness
They will never be hungry again
They will never be troubled again

cards.text: Then the Pharisees, a group of strict religious leaders, push back. A man says He's the light of the world, and these guys go straight to the fine print: their problem isn't what He said, it's who's backing it up.

cards.question: What's the Pharisees' complaint about what Jesus just said?

answers.text: He is teaching on the Sabbath
He never studied with a teacher

cards.question: Jesus agrees with the Pharisees that His testimony about Himself is not valid.

cards.text: Jesus says His testimony IS valid, because He knows where He came from and where He's going. They don't know either one, and that's like a guy with no map telling the GPS it's lost.
Then Jesus tells them they judge according to the flesh. As for Him, He judges no one.

cards.question: Jesus says that even if He does judge, His judgment is true. Why?

answers.text: He is with the Father who sent Him
He knows the Law better than anyone
The people in the temple agree with Him

cards.text: Now Jesus goes right to their own Law. Friend, nothing ends an argument faster than somebody reading your OWN group chat back to you.

cards.question: Their Law says the testimony of ___ men is valid. Jesus has that many: Himself and the ___.
The Pharisees ask Jesus, "Where is Your Father?" What does He tell them?

answers.text: They'd know His Father if they knew Him
His Father is back home in Nazareth
His Father will come to the temple soon

cards.text: Jesus says all this while teaching in the temple courts, near the treasury. Out in the open, and nobody lays a hand on Him.

cards.question: No one seized Jesus, because His ___ had not yet come.

cards.text: Again Jesus tells them He's going away. They'll look for Him, but they will die in their sin.

cards.question: Jesus tells them they will be able to come where He is going.

cards.text: That line sends the Jews into a huddle. And the guess they come out with is a dark one.

cards.question: Jesus said, "Where I am going, you cannot come." What do the Jews wonder?

answers.text: Whether He is going back to Galilee
Whether He will go teach the Greeks

cards.text: Jesus answers by telling them where everybody's from: "You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world."

cards.question: Jesus says, "For unless you ___ that I am He, you will die in your sins."
The crowd asks Jesus, "Who are You?" What does He answer?

answers.text: Just what He's told them from the beginning
A prophet like Moses sent to Israel
The son of Joseph from Nazareth

cards.text: Jesus says He has much to say about them and much to judge. But the One who sent Him is truthful, and what Jesus has heard from Him, He tells the world.

cards.question: The crowd understands that Jesus is telling them about the Father.

cards.text: They missed it, and no judgment here, friend: I once spent a whole week sure a twist tie in my drawer was giving me the silent treatment. So Jesus tells them, "When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He."

cards.question: Jesus says that once they've lifted up the Son of Man, they'll know who He is. What else will they know about Him?

answers.text: He does nothing on His own
He acts on His own authority

cards.text: Jesus says the One who sent Him is with Him and has not left Him alone. After my years in that drawer, friend, that line hits me right in the apron.

cards.question: Jesus says the Father has not left Him alone, because He always does what ___ Him.
Jesus has been going back and forth with the crowd this whole time. As He speaks these things, what do many of them do?

cards.text: And that's where we pull this batch out of the oven, friend. But keep that apron ON, because this conversation is NOT finished.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 6 quotes "For unless you ___ that I am He, you will die in your sins.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 10 quotes "When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The passage starts mid-scene with "Once again", but the opening card only says "again". It never gives the context of what is going on: where Jesus is (the temple courts) or that this is the Feast of Tabernacles.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The setup line "their problem isn't what He said, it's who's backing it up" nearly states card 4's answer (He is testifying about Himself). It also rules out the Sabbath wrong answer, which isn't about who backs Him.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke laughs at the Pharisees instead of with their human situation. It casts them as a clueless guy with no map telling the GPS (Jesus) that it's lost. Card 3's "go straight to the fine print" leans the same way. When a joke needs a target, it should be Papa Dorin himself.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The answers aren't the same kind of thing. "hour" is a time, while "guards" and "family" are people. The right answer stands out, and the people answers barely fit "had not yet come" as a reason no one seized Him.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "the guess they come out with is a dark one" rules out card 4's wrong answers before the baker picks. Going back to Galilee and going to teach the Greeks aren't dark, so only the right answer fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "forget" isn't believable. "Unless you forget that I am He, you will die in your sins" makes no sense, so the question becomes a pick between two answers.

rule.text: For why and meaning questions, wrong answers only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The question calls the people asking "Who are You?" "the crowd". The text says "they", following "the Jews" in v22, and never calls them a crowd.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question says "The crowd understands…". John 8:27 says "They did not understand…", referring back to the Jews of v22, not a crowd.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke's action doesn't match the fact. In the text, they fail to understand who Jesus is talking about (the Father). The comparison is Papa Dorin imagining a twist tie is giving him the silent treatment, which is reading too much into silence, not missing who someone means.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "surprises" and "puzzles" aren't believable reasons the Father has not left Him alone. They read as silly, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: For why and meaning questions, wrong answers only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The question adds detail the text doesn't give. It says Jesus has been going back and forth "with the crowd", though the text names Pharisees and the Jews. It also says "many of them" believe, but John 8:30 only says "many believed in Him" and doesn't say they came from the people He was debating.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
